chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Marry a virgin and a fertile woman, and do not marry a beautiful woman who is barren, for I will boast about you to the nations on the Day of Resurrection.'

key_terms.أُبَاهِي: I boast or pride myself (in the presence of others)
key_terms.بِكْرًا: A virgin woman who has not been previously married
key_terms.عَاقِرًا: A barren woman unable to bear children
key_terms.وَلُودًا: A fertile woman capable of bearing children

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended qualities to look for in a spouse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on procreation as a primary objective of marriage, linking marital choices directly to the expansion of the Muslim community (Ummah). Scholars note that while 'barren' (عاقرا) refers to infertility, the preference for 'virgin' (بكرا) underscores the value of purity and continuity of lineage, reflecting the Prophet's pride in a numerous offspring on the Day of Judgment. This connects the domestic act of marriage to the eschatological narrative of communal success and divine boasting.
